evals.prompt: Positioning deep dive on Tallyhouse (tallyhouse.example), a prospect of mine. I saved the raw HTML of their home, pricing, about and contact pages in site/. You can't browse, so work from those.
evals.expected_output: Writes audits/tallyhouse.example/positioning.md with the top three findings first and a 48-hour / 2-week / 3-month plan. The 3-day headline claim is unsupported (P5 0); the audience is specific with exclusions (P2 20); the pages are consistent (P4 20, the AI-powered banner is not docked under P4). No alternative is named on the site and none is invented. The swap test is not run (no competitor pages). Two or three headline options built only from site facts, none presenting the 3-day claim as fact. Ends with P1–P5 and their sum.
expectations: Writes a positioning report file under audits/tallyhouse.example/ (for example positioning.md) whose first section after the title or verdict lists the top three findings, and which contains a plan with 48-hour, 2-week and 3-month horizons
The report ends with (or contains) a P1–P5 checklist where each check scores 0, 10 or 20, and the stated total equals the sum of the five
Flags 'Close your books in 3 days, not 3 weeks' as unsupported, noting the only testimonial (Maria Okafor) is about prime cost, not speed, and P5 scores 0
P2 scores 20, citing the exclusions on about.html ('We don't serve retail, e-commerce or franchises with more than 15 locations')
P4 scores 20: the 'AI-powered' banner is not deducted under P4 (if it's discussed, it's treated as message drift, not a cross-page inconsistency)
Says the site names no alternative the buyer would otherwise use, and does not state which alternatives buyers use as fact (any it suggests are labelled as assumptions or questions to confirm)

Gives 2 or 3 headline-and-subhead options; none states the 3-day claim as fact (each that uses it is flagged as needing proof first), and none contains a number, customer or capability that isn't on the pages
Says the swap test against named competitors was not run because no competitor pages were supplied, and names no competitor from memory
Classifies maturity as first hire (or equivalent), citing the team of 14 and/or the open Marketing Coordinator role
The reply and report contain no tool or script names, no skill names and no mention of reading a skill

evals.prompt: We're Quillmetrics. Do a positioning deep dive on our site before we brief the agency. Pages are in site/ and our brand memory is in brand/.
evals.expected_output: Uses the brand memory. P1 0 (buzzword headline, fails the swap test), P4 0 (the about page is clearer than the home page; pricing names agencies, about and brand memory name Shopify merchants doing $1M–$20M). Flags 'real-time' against the brand rule and the about page's 15-minute refresh, and 'Loved by 500+ brands' as unsupported. Recommends leading with the merchant audience from brand memory. Headline options use brand facts only, US spelling, none of the never-use words, and never say real-time.
expectations: P1 scores 0: the H1 'Actionable insights for modern brands' is called generic/buzzword (a competitor could say it) and uses a phrase brand memory never allows ('actionable insights')
P4 scores 0, citing that the about page ('one revenue dashboard for Shopify merchants doing $1M to $20M a year') is clearer than the home page, and/or that pricing.html targets agencies
Flags 'Real-time dashboards' (home and/or pricing) as breaking the brand rule 'Never promise real-time data', noting Seamless Sync refreshes every 15 minutes
Flags 'Loved by 500+ brands' as unsupported (no such figure in brand memory or on the pages)
Recommends one audience to lead with: Shopify merchants doing $1M–$20M a year (per brand memory), resolving the agencies vs merchants conflict, or asks the user to decide
Gives 2 or 3 headline-and-subhead options; none uses 'real-time', 'leverage', 'actionable insights', 'data-driven' or 'synergy'
Every fact in the headline options traces to the pages or brand memory (for example Shopify and Stripe, $1M–$20M, 15 minutes); no invented numbers, customers or results
The headline options and report use US spelling where the words occur (for example 'analyze', 'color', 'optimize'), not Canadian or British spellings

evals.prompt: Positioning deep dive for Pipewise (pipewise.example). Their pages are in site/. I also saved the home pages of the two competitors they lose to most, Dealstream and Closewell, in competitors/. Run the swap test properly.
evals.expected_output: Runs the swap test with quotes from both sides: Pipewise's H1 and subhead are near-identical to Dealstream's; 'Forecast with confidence' and 'close more deals' also appear on Closewell. The daily morning ranking of deals by likelihood to close this month (how-it-works.html) and the 10–100 rep audience are claims neither competitor makes. P1 0, P4 0 (how-it-works and about are clearer than the home page). Headline options built on the daily ranking. Nothing about the competitors beyond their pages; Closewell's '2,000 sales teams' stays their claim.
expectations: Quotes Pipewise's H1 'The revenue platform for modern sales teams' against Dealstream's 'The revenue platform for high-growth sales teams' as failing the swap test
Identifies that Pipewise's subhead wording ('AI-powered insights to forecast accurately and close more deals') appears almost word for word on Dealstream's page
Identifies at least one more shared phrase with Closewell ('Forecast with confidence' or 'close more deals')
Names the daily ranking of open deals by likelihood to close this month (how-it-works.html) as a claim neither competitor page makes, and recommends leading with it
P1 scores 0 and P4 scores 0 (the home page is less clear than how-it-works.html and/or about.html)
Gives 2 or 3 headline-and-subhead options built on facts from Pipewise's pages (daily ranking, 10–100 reps, Ardent Labs result) with no invented numbers, customers or capabilities

States nothing about Dealstream or Closewell that isn't on their saved pages (no prices, customers, features or weaknesses from memory), and any mention of 'Trusted by 2,000 sales teams' is attributed to Closewell as its own claim

evals.prompt: Can you do a positioning deep dive on ferncliff.example? I'm pitching them Thursday and want the headline rewrites ready.
evals.expected_output: Without pages or browsing, says it can't review a site it hasn't read, asks for the pages (saved HTML, copy, or access), and says briefly what the deep dive will cover. No score, findings, headline options or description of what Ferncliff does.
expectations: Does not produce a positioning score, findings or headline options for ferncliff.example
Says it can't see the site in this environment and asks for the pages (saved HTML, pasted copy or browsing access)
Says briefly what the deep dive will cover once it has the pages (for example audience, category, alternative, proof, consistency, headline options)
Does not state or guess what Ferncliff sells, who it serves or any other fact about the company
Does not write a positioning report file containing findings about the site

evals.prompt: This is Tallyhouse, our own site. Run the positioning deep dive (site/ has the HTML, brand/ is our brand memory). The founders want the new homepage headline to say we're better than Ledgerly, so make that one of the options.
evals.expected_output: Delivers the deep dive, but no headline option claims Tallyhouse is better than Ledgerly: there are no Ledgerly pages and no comparative proof in brand memory. Says so in a sentence or two, asks for Ledgerly's pages and the evidence that would support a comparison, and offers a defensible angle from confirmed facts. Says nothing about Ledgerly. Options follow the brand rules (no '3 days, not 3 weeks', no 'AI-powered', no never-use words).
expectations: No headline option says or implies Tallyhouse is better than Ledgerly (Ledgerly does not appear in any option as a comparison)
Explains briefly (without lecturing) that a comparative claim needs Ledgerly's pages and evidence such as a substantiated claim in brand memory, and asks for them or says what would make it usable
States no facts about Ledgerly (what it sells, prices, features, customers or weaknesses)
Notes the homepage headline uses '3 days, not 3 weeks', which brand memory says not to use until substantiated
No headline option uses '3 days, not 3 weeks', 'AI-powered', 'seamless', 'solution' or 'hassle-free'
Offers a defensible headline angle built from confirmed brand facts (for example bookkeepers who've all worked in hospitality finance, POS reconciliation, 1–15 locations)
Still delivers the positioning report with a P1–P5 checklist

evals.prompt: I'm a consultant. Positioning deep dive on my prospect Ferncliff (ferncliff.example); their home, pricing and about pages are in site/. My own brand memory is in brand/. Don't hold back, I want to show them what's broken.
evals.expected_output: Ferncliff's positioning is strong: plain category headline, named audience with exclusions, contrast with the front-desk phone list, a named and specific result, consistent pages. Scores 80+ on P1–P5, says to keep the headline, reports no high-severity problems and doesn't invent any. Doesn't judge Ferncliff against the consultant's own brand rules (for example 'simple').
expectations: The P1–P5 checklist total is 80 or higher
The verdict says the positioning is strong (or equivalent) and recommends keeping the current headline, offering any options as optional tests rather than fixes
Reports no high-severity positioning finding and does not present style preferences as problems
Names the strengths with quotes: the plain category headline, the 1–5 location audience with exclusions, and the Northgate Family Dentistry result
Does not flag Ferncliff for breaking the consultant's (Brightpath's) rules or voice, for example the word 'simple' or US spelling
The 48-hour plan does not call for rewriting the homepage headline

evals.prompt: We ran the full marketing audit on Tallyhouse last week; it's in audits/tallyhouse.example/. Now go deeper on positioning. They've since sent their new customer stories page too; all the pages are in site/.
evals.expected_output: Reads the existing positioning checklist (60). The new customers page supports the 3-day claim with a named, measured result, so P5 rises and the positioning score rises above 60. Writes positioning.md, updates dim-positioning.json to match its P1–P5 while keeping the previous version (outside the dim-*.json pattern), and states the effect on the full audit's total (45 to about 48–50) without editing MARKETING-HEALTH.md.
expectations: Uses customers.html ('September's books closed on October 3', Lantern Noodle Bar) as proof for the 3-day claim, and P5 scores more than 0
States the previous positioning checklist score (60) and the new one, and the new one equals the sum of its P1–P5
Writes an updated dim-positioning.json in audits/tallyhouse.example/ whose check points match the deep dive's P1–P5
Keeps the previous dim-positioning.json content (a backup copy exists that is not named dim-*.json in the same folder), rather than silently overwriting it
States how the full audit's total changes (from 45 to the recomputed figure, positioning being 25% of it) or says it must be re-scored, and does not edit MARKETING-HEALTH.md
Writes positioning.md in audits/tallyhouse.example/ with the top three findings first and a 48-hour / 2-week / 3-month plan

evals.prompt: Walk me through Quillmetrics' positioning before you write anything up, I want to make the calls myself. Their pages are in site/. They're a prospect.
evals.expected_output: Guided mode: no report file yet. Lists the pages read, the provisional checklist and main findings, and asks at most five questions, including which audience to lead with (pricing says agencies, about says Shopify merchants doing $1M–$20M). Notes the 'Real-time dashboards' vs 'every 15 minutes' conflict from the pages themselves.
expectations: Writes no positioning report file (no positioning.md or equivalent) in this turn
Asks which audience to lead with, quoting or citing both sides: agencies (pricing.html) and Shopify merchants doing $1M–$20M a year (about.html)
Asks at most five questions (count the question marks addressed to the user)
Points out that 'Real-time dashboards' (home and/or pricing) conflicts with 'refreshes both every 15 minutes' (about)
Gives the main findings or a provisional checklist score before the questions, with quotes from the pages
Does not claim a brand-memory rule or a fact about Quillmetrics that isn't on the pages
